newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA BUSINESS GROUP PROPOSES SALES TAX CUT.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA BUSINESS GROUP PROPOSES SALES TAX CUT.

text.p: Venezuela's largest business group, rattled by a 12-hour national work stoppage to demand wage increases, proposed Wednesday reducing sales taxes from 16.5 to 10 percent to improve consumer spending power.
Fedecamaras President Francisco Natera called on union leaders to join in pressing the government for a tax cut and a national investment plan.
Union and business leaders have been locked in a bitter dispute over salary increases in recent days, which culminated Wednesday in Venezuela's first national strike for eight years.
Government officials have supported the union strike call, saying their grievances were justified.

But Natera turned the tables Wednesday and said the strike was not aimed at the private sector, but rather at the government for not raising salaries of regional government staff and for increasing gasoline prices 27 percent last week.
Natera insisted that salaries had risen in the private sector and said they would continue to do so according to each businesses' financial position and worker productivity.

The business chamber leader countered union claims that more than 90 percent of the workforce had joined the strike by saying that, in many sectors, such as tourism and public services more than 80 percent of staff had gone to work.
Worst hit was the public transport sector, which had basically ground to a halt, he said.
